fields.meta_description: Describe your approval limits and pay days. Emergent builds accounts payable automation from the AP inbox to the payment run. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build Accounts Payable Automation From Inbox to Paid
fields.hero_description: Describe who signs off at which amount and the day you pay suppliers. Emergent builds the app that runs your AP inbox on those rules, and changes it when the policy does.
fields.features_subheading: Accounts payable automation moves a supplier invoice from inbox to paid without anyone retyping it. People see only the exceptions.
fields.feature_1:
Invoice capture from email and uploads

A PDF in the AP inbox or an upload from a vendor portal is read into fields, from the vendor and invoice number down to each line item. Low-confidence fields wait for a person.
fields.feature_2:
Two-way and three-way matching

Each invoice is checked against its purchase order and goods receipt. When a unit price or a received quantity disagrees, the invoice is held and the buyer sees the difference.
fields.feature_3:
Approval routing by amount and vendor

Bills route by amount, vendor, entity, or GL code, and the request lands in Slack or email. A reminder follows after two days. A missed deadline escalates to a backup approver.
fields.feature_4:
Payment runs on your schedule

Approved bills are batched into weekly or early-pay runs and released through the bank file or payments API you connect, on the payment dates finance sets in advance.
fields.feature_5:
Posted to your accounting system

Each approved bill posts to QuickBooks, Xero, or NetSuite with its GL code and a link back to the source PDF. Once a payment run is released, each payment posts against its bill.
fields.feature_6:
Code in your repo, data in your database

The matching rules and the approval chain export to your GitHub repository as code your engineers can review. Bill and payment records sit in your own database, one row per bill.
fields.why_title: Why Build Your AP Automation With Emergent?
fields.why_description: In an AP suite, your approval rules live inside the vendor's app. With Emergent they are code in your repo, changed by prompting.

fields.usecase_heading: AP Automation Workflows to Build Today
fields.tab_content_1:
Match every invoice to its PO before it reaches an approver

Northwind's invoice for brackets and fasteners is matched line by line to PO-3107 and the goods receipt. A price or quantity outside the tolerance holds it and sends the difference to the buyer. Clean matches go to the budget owner, and a bill posts to NetSuite once it is approved.
fields.tab_content_2:
Pay recurring bills on time without a reminder spreadsheet

Rent and software subscriptions arrive as recurring bills. Each is compared with last month's amount. A bill that rises by more than a tenth waits for the department head. The rest join Friday's payment run without a review.
fields.tab_content_3:
Route each entity's bills to its own controller

The billing address printed on an invoice decides which company it belongs to, and the bill goes to that entity's controller for approval. Acme Ltd pays its bills from the GBP account and Acme GmbH from the EUR account. One dashboard splits the month's spend by entity for the close.
fields.tab_content_4:
Pay contractors once their paperwork is complete

Contractors submit invoices from a phone, and each one is checked against the contract rate. W-9 and bank details are collected once and verified on every submission. Approved invoices join the biweekly Friday payout. Every payment record stays ready for 1099 season.

fields.howto_description: Most of the work is writing down the rules your controller already applies and picking a pay day. Seven steps take that policy from a document to a live AP inbox.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Map how invoices reach you today
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put the approval rules in writing
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every way invoices arrive today, from the shared AP inbox to paper bills scanned at the front desk and contractor emails sent to whoever hired them. Note who touches each one and where it waits. That map becomes the intake and the first routing rules.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Describe the policy the way your controller would say it: anything over $10,000 goes to the CFO, and a new software vendor needs procurement first. Add the exceptions too, such as who signs when the CFO is away. Emergent turns those sentences into routing rules.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose two-way matching for services and three-way matching for goods you receive. Then set how far a unit price or a received quantity may drift from the PO before the invoice is held for the buyer.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect the accounting system your team closes the books in, from QuickBooks to any ERP with an API. Vendor records and open purchase orders come in, and approved bills go back out. GL coding suggestions are drawn from how your team coded the same vendor before.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick your payment days and the bank file or payments API that releases the money. A vendor offering 2/10 net 30 can go into an early-pay run before the tenth day. Every other approved bill waits for the regular Friday run.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run last month's invoices through the workflow before go-live and set its decisions beside what your team did by hand. Where a route or a GL code disagrees, fix the rule by prompting and run the sample again until the two match.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Go live and watch cycle time
fields.howto_step_7_des: Point the AP inbox at the workflow and keep the old process as a fallback for one payment cycle. The dashboard tracks the days from invoice to payment and the share of bills held. Every rule change is versioned in your repo.
